messages:
marcus: Heads-up — ran into a compliance snag: a customer in healthcare asked us to guarantee that certain request fields never land in our telemetry exporters (traces/OTLP). They want per-route opt-out flags and strong audit trails. Thoughts?
lila: +1 on opt-out. Do we mean: (a) never collect those attributes at instrumentation time, or (b) collect but redact before export? Different risk profiles.
prashant: They probably want assurance for e2e: ideally we don't persist sensitive text anywhere. My vote is 'don't collect' unless explicitly allowed by config. Easier for audits + GDPR/PHI.
marcus: Agree. But 'don't collect' reduces debugability. Some of our infra folks use spans to triage timeouts. We need a mechanism to gate attributes so ops can opt-in per-service/route, and every change requires an audit entry.
anya: We should model this as two orthogonal controls: sampling/collection policy + exporter gating. Config idea: service.yaml -> telemetry: attributes: deny_list: ["user_input","prompt_text"] allow_list: [] opt_out_routes: ["/v1/claims"]
prashant: That works. Also need enforcement at the SDK + collector. If SDK tags attribute as sensitive, collector must drop it before any storage or exporter. We can add an attribute: "redaction.level" = "drop|pseudonymize|hash" settable by policy.
lila: What about pseudonymization? Some teams want identifiers for linking but not raw values. If we hash with a per-tenant salt stored in KMS, we can avoid reversible mapping. Key rotation becomes tricky though.
marcus: Good point. For deterministic pseudonymization we need a stable key per-tenant. KMS/HSM for key material + rotation policy. Audit log entry whenever a key is rotated or used for pseudonymization.
telemetry-bot: Reminder: existing exporters (bigquery, datadog, internal-telemetry-store) expect OTLP attributes unchanged. We'll need exporter adapters that enforce policy and record audit events.
prashant: Proposed minimal design: 1) SDK: mark attributes with meta flag e.g., set_attribute("prompt_text", value, {sensitive: true}) 2) Collector: policy engine consults route/service config and either drops/pseudonymizes/hash 3) Exporters: only receive post-policy attributes, and emit an audit record to audit-telemetry.
marcus: Example pseudo-config: ```yaml
telemetry_policy:
  defaults:
    prompt_text: drop
    user_email: pseudonymize
  routes:
    "/v1/claims":
      prompt_text: drop
      debug_ids: allow
  audit_sink: "gs://redwood-telemetry-audit"
```
anya: Also need retention rules: even pseudonymized attributes should obey retention windows. For example, keep hash for 90 days then truncate. That should be part of the exporter contract.
lila: Operational concerns: If we drop attributes upstream, SRE will lose context. Maybe introduce a 'secure debug' workflow: ability for authorized users to request temporary unredacted traces (requires approval + audit + TTL).
marcus: I like secure debug. Implementation sketch: when someone requests, system checks RBAC, spins up a short-lived reingestion job that reads from an encrypted staging bucket and returns unredacted spans for that trace id, flagged in audit. TTL enforced.
prashant: Security: export encryption at rest is table stakes. For pseudonymization keys use per-tenant KMS keys. Access to plaintext should require a decrypt permission and be logged.
anya: Testing: need unit tests + canaries where collector runs with a 'safe' mode that simulates drop/pseudonymize and emits metrics on how many attributes would be redacted. Useful for migration.
lila: UX: console should show per-route telemetry policy, last change + who changed it, and a 'what-if' toggle to preview effect on recent traces. Also surface failed exporter deliveries if gating blocks everything.
marcus: Action items: 1) prashant to draft SDK attr tagging API (ETA 1 week) 2) anya to prototype collector policy engine + canary mode (ETA 2w) 3) lila to mock console UX + audit timeline (ETA 1w) 4) infra to confirm KMS/HSM constraints (pinging infra).
prashant: Will start SDK RFC. One design question: should SDK do client-side redaction by default when flagged sensitive? Or leave to collector? My preference: tag at SDK and optionally drop client-side when route annotated as no-telemetry.
marcus: Okay — if SDK can drop client-side when configured, that reduces blast radius and simplifies compliance. But we must ensure SDK config updates are propagated quickly.
lila: I'll add secure-debug flow to the UX mock. Also propose a retention tab showing counts of redacted vs retained attributes.
marcus: Thanks all. @infra-team can you weigh in on KMS and audit log storage for the prototype? :pray:
telemetry-bot: infra-team notifies: @infra oncall — please review KMS/key rotation feasibility for per-tenant pseudonymization (ref: ticket INF-4921).
